body: Quick pass: merges cleanly with main, author's quick gate green on 606dc614 (pins in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/gcode_viewer.rs`), body complete, no snapshot PNG touched. Flagged ready for the independent review. Stacked on #955: merge that first.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 606dc614ce4f337a876fb32559ca46cb0b249211 -->
**Needs changes before merge** (one blocker, small fix). Stacked on #955: merge that first.

**Read and run**
- Read the PR's own commits (29878eb5, 606dc614) against #955's head, plus the trial merge of current main (clean, no conflicts). `gcode_view.rs` (new, moved from `pages.rs`), `gcode_highlight.rs` (`gutter_text`), `shell.rs`, `mod.rs`, `tests/gcode_viewer.rs`, `docs/decisions/1089-gcode-window.md`.
- The PR's own commits touch no snapshot PNG (the PNG changes in the branch diff come from main's ad407f8c).
- Local results on the trial merge:
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib gcode`: 13 passed, 0 failed (gcode_viewer: 6 incl. click, cursor highlight, copy, trace width; gcode_highlight: 5; gcode_segment: 1; plus theme/word tests).
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib structural`: 4 passed, 0 failed.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

**Looks good**
- Issue items 1, 2, 4 are in place: the gutter is a non-selectable label, the code is selectable (copy takes code only); the cursor row gets a fill; trace-on uses fixed rects, so the window keeps its size.
- Click path: `bg.clicked() || code.clicked()` covers the whole row. `jump` is queued and applied next frame. Index math has no panic path: `saturating_sub`, `min`, `get(i)`, and `position` on `blocks`. The float-to-usize casts are clamped with `max(0.0)` first.
- The wheel/scrollbar release is right: a pin is dropped as soon as the settled middle row changes (`_ => remove`), so ordinary scrolling returns the cursor to the middle row. It is untested, see note 2.

**Requested before merge**
1. **Stale click pin can point past the end of a new listing** (`gcode_view.rs`, `gcode_listing`, the `pin` match near `*line = match pin`). The pin `(row, middle)` lives in egui temp memory under `PIN_ID`. Nothing clears it when `PostView` is replaced by a new post, and the row is never clamped on read. The pin is only dropped when the middle row changes, so a replacement program whose middle row happens to match the old one keeps the old row. If that row is past the new program's end, `line` is out of range: no row is highlighted, the trace shows nothing, and the amber segment only clamps by accident (`shell.rs:842`). No panic, but it is a silent wrong cursor, and the issue asks for exactly this cursor to be right. Fix: (a) clamp on read: `Some((r, m)) if m == mid => r.min(n.saturating_sub(1))`, and store the clamped row; (b) clear `PIN_ID` when the listing changes, e.g. store the program's line count (or a cheap hash) with the pin and drop the pin on mismatch. Add a test: click row 290 of a 300-line program, post a 30-line program with the same middle, assert the cursor is in `0..30` and some row is highlighted.
2. Formatting: `gcode_view.rs` has a stray over-indented `}` after `jump.set(Some(i));` in `gcode_listing`, and `area.show` is indented one level too deep. Run rustfmt on the file.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- Untested paths, all read as right in the code: wheel or scrollbar releases the pin (note: a scroll that keeps the middle row keeps the pin, which is intended); close and reopen (pin survives in egui memory and the scroll offset is kept by id `gcode-scroll`); resize that changes the middle row releases the pin; an empty listing (`n = 0`, clamps to row 0, no highlight) and a one-line program are safe by the same clamps. Worth one test each, especially the empty and one-line cases.
- `pages.rs` shrinks by the moved viewer; `gcode_view.rs` is 285 lines, under the ~400 limit.
- Plain English checked: "WARNING:", "G-code", "trace", "Ctrl+C" text is fine.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: dddd9b0b07c8664bffc800333bf666e66ce58db0 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** The blocker from the last review is closed. Stacked on #955: merge that first.

**Delta reviewed:** `git diff 606dc614..dddd9b0b` (`gcode_view.rs`, `gcode_highlight.rs` `program_key`, `tests/gcode_viewer.rs`). Trial merge with current main is clean.

**Results (trial merge, head dddd9b0b)**
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib gcode`: 15 passed, 0 failed (the two new tests included).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib structural`: 4 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No snapshot PNG in the delta. `gcode_view.rs` is 293 lines.

**Blocker check**
- The read path is now `filter(key == program_key)` then `.map(r.min(last))`. Whatever pin survives, its row is clamped to the new listing, so `line` is always `<= last` and no index can pass the end. Empty listing: `last = 0`, row 0, no highlight, safe. One line: safe.
- A new post with a different length, or a closed viewer, drops the pin. Good.
- `program_key` collisions (same length, same first and last 256 bytes, different middle): the pin stays, and its row is a valid row of an equally long listing. Highlight, cursor and amber segment stay consistent with each other. It is not a wrong cursor in any harmful sense: the row is the line number the user clicked. Note only.
- No new panic path: `b[..min(256)]` and `b[len.saturating_sub(256)..]` cannot go out of range.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. The two new tests pass even with the fix removed. I checked this by reverting the key filter and the clamp locally (not committed) and running both: `a_click_pin_does_not_outlive_its_listing` and `a_wheel_scroll_after_a_click_releases_the_pin` still pass. The 20/1/0-line replacement moves the middle row away from the pinned one, so the old pin is released by the scroll anyway. A test that pins the fix needs a replacement whose settled middle row equals the old one (e.g. a 300-to-290-line program clicked at its bottom). Worth a follow-up, not a merge blocker.
2. `set_program` and `a_click_pin...` build the program string with a literal newline inside `join("` ... `")`. It works (the string is `\n`), but `"\n"` reads better. Style only.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
